Discovered + fixed one real backend bug in /app/backend/routes/browse.py (operator-precedence bug ignored explicit device_id from request body). After fix: 17/17 PASS (100%).

minor.issue: FIXED — Original code at routes/browse.py:318 used `data.get('device_id') or data.get('device_info', {}).get('device_id') if isinstance(data.get('device_info'), dict) else None`. Due to Python operator precedence (`or` binds tighter than ternary `if/else`), the whole expression resolved to None whenever `device_info` was absent or non-dict — meaning the explicit `device_id` field in the request body was silently ignored and the server always generated a fresh `web_xxxxxx` ID. Symptom: native-app callers couldn't keep a stable device fingerprint; devices[] would balloon on every play. Replaced with an explicit if/elif/if block.

critical_code_review_comments: FIXED during this run: routes/browse.py device_id ternary precedence bug (see backend_issues.minor).

Defaults['minimum_payout'] in core/play_analytics.py is short-circuited together with revenue when billing_enabled=False. That's correct, but the response still returns the minimum_payout in `rates`. If a UI conditionally hides the payout button based on `rates.minimum_payout`, double-check it also respects `billing_enabled` to avoid showing 'min payout: 10,000 TZS' on an unbilled account.

core/play_analytics.py L195-197: when billing_enabled=False we zero current_balance/total_earned/total_withdrawn from the account doc. If billing is later turned back on, the stored account.current_balance still reflects pre-toggle reality — confirm there's a reconciliation job, otherwise re-enabling billing instantly shows back any previously-accrued balance (which may be desired, but worth documenting).

routes/analytics.py /analytics/realtime aggregates `device_brand` from in-memory active_streams data — perfectly fine for live view. The companion /analytics/devices aggregates from listening_sessions over the full window with $facet — also good, but consider an index on listening_sessions.start_time + device_brand to keep the 30d/90d facet under 200ms as data grows.

routes/browse.py listening/start: the location $push uses `$slice: -50` (keep last 50). When the doc has no `locations` field yet, MongoDB treats $push+$slice on an absent field correctly (creates new array, slices last 50). Verified — no issue. Good defensive choice.

rca of the issue: RCA — device_id from body ignored: /app/backend/routes/browse.py:318 used `data.get('device_id') or data.get('device_info', {}).get('device_id') if isinstance(data.get('device_info'), dict) else None`. Python operator precedence binds `or` tighter than the conditional expression `X if Y else Z`, so the whole left side was only evaluated when device_info was a dict; otherwise it short-circuited to None, ignoring an explicit `device_id` in the JSON body. Mitigation applied: rewrote as explicit if/elif/if block so explicit device_id always wins, with device_info as a fallback and a generated `web_xxxxxx` ID as the final fallback. Verified by re-running the dedupe test — the same device_id no longer creates duplicate devices[] entries on app_users.
